purpose: Multilingual lexicon for the dimension values of config/divinity_ontology.json. A value is attested in a work when an entry of that value matches in a language the work's sources are written in, or when an English surface pattern matches AND the entry's translation-equivalence claim is marked verified.
status: SEARCH-CANDIDATE LAYER ONLY. Every entry below is `unverified_secondary_literature` except where marked. Per the ontology's verification_rule, unverified entries may generate candidates for a human coder and must never be counted as attestations. Dates are the range conventionally assigned to the earliest surviving textual occurrence, not to the concept's origin, which is not datable.
date_convention: BCE/CE integers; `attested_from` = earliest surviving witness carrying this expression with this sense; `date_basis` = the kind of argument the date rests on and therefore how far it can be trusted

entries.gloss: deity; sky; also the determinative prefixed to divine names
entries.source_text: Fara and Abu Salabikh god lists
entries.reference: a god-list handbook or ETCSL entry should be cited before use
entries.caution: the determinative survives into Akkadian texts where the word is not read; determinative occurrences are not attestations of a concept

entries.gloss: 'lord wind'; head of the Nippur pantheon, decree-holder
entries.reference: the Ouehli-Tab editions and ETCSL catalogue
entries.caution: supremacy here is textual-political and tracks Nippur's prestige; treating it as a concept of 'a supreme god' generalises one city's cult

entries.gloss: god, a member of the class of gods
entries.source_text: Old Babylonian royal inscriptions; Enuma Elish
entries.reference: CAD volume I; a dictionary citation is required
entries.caution: cognate with Hebrew eloah and Arabic ilah; the cognate is evidence of a shared word, not of a shared concept, and genealogies of vocabulary are exactly what M1 and M3 predict differently

entries.gloss: god; possibly 'that which is to be feared'
entries.reference: the Pyramid Texts editions and a lexicon entry
entries.caution: the etymology is contested; etymological speculation must not be coded as an ontology claim

entries.gloss: god / gods; morphologically plural, frequently singular in reference
entries.date_basis: latest common dating range for the transmitted books; composition dating is unresolved
entries.reference: a critical edition (BHS) with page and line
entries.caution: the plural form has been read as a plurality trace and as an intensive singular; the KJV renders it 'God' throughout, which silently settles the question in English. Never code a Hebrew plurality claim from an English Bible.

entries.expression: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהוָה אֶחָד
entries.gloss: Deut 6:4; 'eḥad' is disputed between 'one', 'unique' and 'alone'
entries.reference: BHS critical apparatus plus a commentary on the eḥad/yaḥid question
entries.caution: the Targum renders it 'the Lord is one', the Shema's oneness has been read monolatrously and monotheistically for two thousand years; the English 'is one LORD' is a translation decision, which is why this entry maps to a value rather than confirming a doctrine

entries.gloss: god; also used of an abstraction or a divinity in general
entries.reference: LSJ entry with cited occurrences
entries.caution: the same word serves the philosophers' impersonal first principle, so a Greek 'theos' does not decide D1

entries.gloss: fate as an order binding even gods
entries.reference: a Stoic sources collection
entries.caution: Fate here outranks Zeus in some passages and is his instrument in others; that is a D2 disagreement inside one tradition, and a strong warning against treating a tradition as internally consistent

entries.gloss: god
entries.reference: OLD or Lewis-Short entry
entries.caution: Varro's tripartite theology (mythical, physical, civic) is an explicit ancient classification of divine-concept types, which is annotation by the source itself and outranks any modern coding of the same material

entries.gloss: lord, mighty one; in the Rigveda often of high gods, later of demons
entries.date_basis: the most widely used (and contested) composition window for the mandalas
entries.reference: an edition with mandala and hymn number, e.g. Jamison-Brereton
entries.caution: the asura/deva reversal is a textbook instance of the `demotion` operator, and it is dated on literary stratigraphy alone; it should be coded as a transformation candidate, not a documented transformation

entries.gloss: shining one, god; a class member rather than a supreme term
entries.reference: Monier-Williams with Rigveda citations
entries.caution: cognate with deus and Zeus; the cognate set tells us about Proto-Indo-European vocabulary, which is a much earlier and much weaker claim than a shared divine concept

entries.gloss: sacred utterance, then the ground of all being; distinct from brahma (masc.), the god
entries.reference: a critical Upanishad edition with passage number
entries.caution: the neuter/masculine distinction is invisible in English 'Brahman' and is exactly the `nominalisation` operator in action; the Gita and the Upanishads differ on whether this ground is personal, so one corpus keyword covers two incompatible D1 values

entries.gloss: a being worthy of worship
entries.date_basis: Gathic dating turns entirely on the linguistic argument, which is unresolved
entries.reference: Koticha or Humbach with Yasna number
entries.caution: the Wilson anthology prints Darmesteter's Zend-Avesta selection; the dating in this entry has nothing to do with what the anthology's nineteenth-century text can support

entries.gloss: cosmic and moral order as such
entries.reference: the Vedic index (van Nooten-Charleston) for the distribution
entries.caution: order is both a principle and, in Varuna, a person; the same content oscillates between D1 values within a single hymn, so `undecidable` is often the honest coding

entries.gloss: law, teaching, the way things are
entries.reference: a Pali edition with chapter and verse
entries.caution: the Buddha's withheld questions about the world's eternity make D6 `undecidable` by doctrine, not by accident; a missing answer is a position

entries.gloss: the creator god, a personification of the neuter ground
entries.reference: a Purana edition with adhyaya number
entries.caution: Puranic creation cycles are measured in kalpas, so D6 here is not 'linear_once'; English summaries flatten that, which is precisely the `silencing` operator

entries.gloss: descent; a deliberate embodiment of a deity
entries.reference: a Gita edition with verse number
entries.caution: 'avatar' in English now means an image and carries no D4 claim at all; a surface-form match on the modern English word is not evidence of anything

entries.gloss: the tawhid formula: there is no deity except He
entries.date_basis: traditional revelation dates; the earliest manuscripts are later, so the witness date and the composition date must be recorded separately
entries.reference: a Muhsaf with surah and verse number; the SBE/quran_sale English rendering is Sale's
entries.caution: the formula is simultaneously the most confident exclusivist assertion in the corpus and a negation, so a naive denial-detector files it under skepticism; v1's exclusion rule handled the shahada but not the conditional and reported-speech cases

entries.gloss: the doctrine of divine oneness
entries.reference: a kalam anthology
entries.caution: oneness argued is a different speech act from oneness confessed; the ontology separates them only through D7

entries.gloss: high sovereign / Heaven as the sanctioning transcendence
entries.date_basis: oracle-bone dating is archaeological and comparatively firm; transmitted-text dates are not
entries.reference: an oracle-bone catalogue number plus a Shijing edition
entries.caution: the Ti/Shangdi terminological debate in the Chinese classics is where the 'celestial bureaucracy' idea was born and where 'Mandate of Heaven' loses its personal agent; the Wilson-era English 'Jade Emperor' is a later folk-imperial projection and must not be read back into the classics

entries.gloss: the way; a generative order without mind or worship
entries.reference: the Guodian or Mawangdui manuscripts with a edition reference
entries.caution: 'Dao' is transliterated, not translated, in most English editions; so it is one of the few concepts this English-only corpus can actually see, which makes it a trap: presence here is an artifact of orthography

entries.gloss: Heaven as sanctioning power whose mandate is revocable by virtue
entries.date_basis: transmitted-text dating, disputed for the earlier layers
entries.reference: a critical Chinese concordance
entries.caution: Heaven here judges dynasties rather than persons, so D4 'judging_moral_order' needs a scope qualifier or the coding will read as a generic moral deity

entries.gloss: a ranged class of revered beings, powers and places
entries.date_basis: dated compilation, describing much earlier material
entries.reference: an annotated Kojiki translation with page
entries.caution: the Kojiki's genealogies make D6 'born_in_time' native to this tradition, which v1 could not express at all; 'god' as translation of kami is a decision with the same weight as a coding

entries.gloss: a member of the divine race / the neutral word for deity
entries.date_basis: manuscript dates, with the oral-material question unresolved
entries.reference: an Edda edition with stanza number
entries.caution: Snorri wrote 600 years after Christianisation and systematises; treating his pantheon as inherited practice is the `editorial_or_ethnographic_description` error at a medieval scale

entries.gloss: the wise lord, opposed to the daēva
entries.reference: Yasna with Humbach's line numbers
entries.caution: Zurvanism makes Time the parent of the twins, adding a D6 'outside_time' layer; the same tradition therefore supplies evidence for two D2 codings, and the anthology text cannot arbitrate

entries.gloss: sacred power, diffused and addressable
entries.source_text: recorded oral tradition, 19th c. ethno-linguistic sources
entries.date_basis: collector documentation; no pre-contact textual witness exists, which is a limit on the tradition's dated attestation, not on the tradition
entries.reference: a dated ethnographic source with the informant noted
entries.caution: 'Great Spirit' is a missionary-era English gloss, so the corpus's evidence for this concept is a translation artifact; also oral tradition's dating cannot be handled by a witness-date field at all

entries.gloss: a spirit, a power; general rather than personal
entries.reference: a dated mission relation or an ethnography with the community named
entries.caution: v1 rejected the bare term 'mana' as a plural of 'man'; the same collision problem applies to 'manitou' in English ethnography. Every Algonquian entry must record community and informant or it becomes one undifferentiated 'native' category

entries.gloss: divine beings in descent lines; tapu as a transferred property
entries.date_basis: printed recording dates; oral antiquity unknown
entries.reference: a dated collection naming the iwi
entries.caution: the Maui cycle has deified-ancestor and culture-hero readings in tension, which is `euhemerisation` live in the tradition's own material

entries.gloss: a consecrated place, object or ancestor requiring reverence
entries.date_basis: colonial documentation, shaped by the question asked
entries.reference: Cobo or an annotated ethnohistory
entries.caution: the extirpation-of-idolatry records describe what they were hunting to destroy; a polemic source is `reported_speech_of_opponent` about a practice, and must not be coded as the practice's own D7 value

entries.gloss: a high god term; 'Elyon' occurs in a psalm context where Melchizedek blesses by 'God Most High'
entries.reference: the Dead Sea reading of Deut 32:8 versus the Masoretic
entries.caution: Deut 32:8-9 as read at Qumran assigns YHWH a share among sons of El, which is the single most-cited Hebrew-Bible case of `elevation` and `scope_expansion`; the English KJV prints the reading that hides it, so this project's own text is the confounder

entries.gloss: sky-god or high god, often remote with delegated spirits
entries.reference: a dated ethnography with the community and informant
entries.caution: the 'deus otiosus' pattern is exactly what M2 and M4 predict in different ways, so coding a remote high god from 1950s ethnography into a Bronze-Age inheritance argument is where this frame must refuse to move

entries.gloss: the 'master of things on the back', and spirit as a ubiquitous power
entries.reference: an annotated monograph
entries.caution: the Dinka 'highest god' problem is a documented collision between an ethnographer's monotheistic expectations and the informant's usage, so coding this as a D2 value is a direct test of whether the frame can see its own instrument's bias

coverage_assessment.consequence: Values with no entry cannot be detected at all, and the instrument must report them as `not_yet_instrumented` rather than `not_attested`. Two of the uninstrumented values — the apophatic negation and the non-divine claimant's boast — are exactly the cases where v1 produced its worst errors, so the frame's weakest points sit directly over the failures it was built to fix.
coverage_assessment.required_before_any_claim: Every entry needs a real citation (edition, page, line) and a coder who can read the script; until then this file is a search plan.
